THE BREAST #1

Breast examination – WHY? #2

  • DIAGNOSTIC (symptoms)
  • - subjective - pain, tension , premenstrual syndrome, cancerophobia
  • - objective – lump (nodule), nipple discharge, skin changes, nipple retraction, asymmetry
  • NO SYMPTOMS
  • - SCREENING (screening programs)
  • - high risk pacientst
  • - control after breast-conserving surgery/of the contralateral breast
  • - metastasis of unknown origin

Breast examination – HOW? #3

  • Mammography – radiography, X rays
  • Ultrasound – 2D (Doppler, elastography)
  • MRI – with contrast

Breast examination – HOW? #4

  • NEVER!!!
  • CT
  • thermography
  • nuclear medicine (treatment YES – sparing breast surgery with santinel node biopsy)
  • http://www.lasvegasthermography.com/services/

Analog or digital mammograhy (2D mammography) #5

  • BREAST EXAMINATION - MAMMOGRAPHY

two standard projections : mediolateral oblic (MLO) and cranio-caudal (CC) #6

  • BREAST EXAMINATION - MAMMOGRAPHY

MLO #7

CC #8

Tomosintesis (3D digital mammography) #9

  • - multiple sections (one breast compresion), different angles, one movement of the X-ray tube on an arch
  • BREAST EXAMINATION - MAMMOGRAPGY

Tomosintesis (3D digital mammography) #10

  • - multiple sections (one breast compresion), different angles, one movement of the X-ray tube on an arch
  • BREAST EXAMINATION - MAMMOGRAPGY

Digital contrast enhenced mammography (CESM) #11

  • - iv contrast media (iodine)
  • - two exposures with different energies
  • - substraction of the images with visualization of the CM only
  • BREAST EXAMINATION - MAMMOGRAPGY

Mammography – Indications #12

  • screening (diagnosis of occult breast cc, women over 40 years)
  • diagnosis (symptomatic patients, over 35 years)
  • Follow-up – patients treated for a breast cc
  • tomosyntesis – supplimentary (patients with dense breast)
  • CESM – could replace MRI (studies) (patients with contraindications for MRI)

Mammography – Limits #13

  • reduced sensitivity in the dense breast
  • reduced sensitivity in the augmented breast
  • difficult to perform in patients with acute inflammation / breast trauma

2D US #14

  • Doppler US
  • Elastography
  • BREAST EXAMINATION - ULTRASOUND

US - Indications #15

  • palpable lumps or mammography anomalies
  • women under 30 years (first step examination)
  • dense breast (white mammography)
  • peripheral lesions
  • guidance of interventional procedures (if visible on US)
  • best method for axillary lymph nodes evaluation

US - Limits #16

  • real time and operator dependent
  • does not allow characterization of microcalcifications associated with breast cancer

highest sensitivity, low specificity #17

  • always with contrast agent
  • malignant lesions have an intense and early contrast uptake and the contrast is rapidly washed out
  • T2, T1 pre and postcontrast
  • BREAST EXAMINATION - MRI

MRI - Indications #18

  • breast cancer staging
  • diagnosis of multicentricity, multifocality or bilaterality
  • differential between recurrence and scar after breast sparing surgery
  • metastasis of unknown primary
  • augmented breast
  • screening for BRCA positive

Slide 19 #19

MRI – Limits #20

  • multiple false positive results
  • false negative results for comedo DCIS (MRI does not depict the typical microcalcifications)
  • long waiting and examination time
  • expensive, feromagnetism, claustrophobia

ANATOMY #21

  • Lobes consist of glandular tissue (lobular), ductal, fatty and fibrous tissue

Imaging – normal appearance #22

  • Adipose tissue – radiolucent / hypoechoic

Imaging – normal appearance #23

  • glandular, ductal and fibrous tissue –
  • radiodense / hyperechoic
  • On Mx and US, these elements cannot be differentiated

Correlation Mx – US #24

  • cancer
  • opaque (WHITE) – on mamo
  • hipoechoic (black) – on US

What is the difference? #25

NORMAL APPEARANCE #26

  • Variations from patient to patient
  • Variations due to physiological status and age
  • ACR – BIRADS (The American College of Radiology – Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System)

Mammography – normal appearance #27

  • BIRADS a-d
  • Significance – tells the clinician that mammography can miss a small cancer in a dense breast (low sensitivity).

Mammographic semeiology #28

  • Asymmetrical density (global/focal)
  • Nodular density (mass)
  • Architectural distorsion
  • Microcalcifications

Mammographic semeiology Asymmetrical density #29

  • Causes:
  • - physiological
  • - focal lesion (mass)
  • - after surgery
  • - incorrect technique

Mammographic semeiology Nodular density #30

  • Analysis:
  • - localization – clock
  • - dimension – progression indicator
  • - shape
  • - contour
  • - density
  • - associated lesions: architectural distorsion, calcifications, skin/nipple changes

Masses #31

  • the only finding

Mammographic semeiology Calcifications #40

  • benign: large, round/oval, with similar size and morphology
  • malignant: small (microcalcifications), irregular, branching (intraductal), heterogeneous in size/shape

US – normal appearance #52

  • skin
  • fatty superficial
  • glandular tissue
  • fatty profound
  • pectoral m.
  • ribs

US semeiology #53

  • shape – regular, irregular
  • contour (margins) – circumscribed noncircumscribed
  • orientation – parallel, perpendicular
  • echogenity – hypo, iso, hyperecogen, anechoic
  • echostructure – homogeneous, inhomogeneous
  • vascularisation – present, absent
  • elasticity – elastic, stiff
  • associated changes: architectural distorsion, skin changes etc

Breast MRI #62

  • T2 – for cystic lesions
  • T1 + SC – for visualization and analysis of the morphology and dynamic behaviour of the lesions

MRI semeiology #63

  • findings:
  • - mass
  • - hypersignal with no associated mass

Mass – description: #64

  • - shape: regular (round or oval) or irregular
  • - contour: : circumscribed or noncircumscibed (ill defined, lobulated or spiculated)
  • - internal signal morfology: homogeneous, heterogeneous, ring
  • - dynamic of the lesions (intensity-time curve): continuous, in plateau, “wash-out”
  • MRI semeiology

Dynamic of the postcontrast hypersignalWash-out or plateauProgressive or plateau

BI-RADS #68

  • 0 – supplementary informations needed
  • 1 – normal
  • 2 – benign lesion
  • 3 – probably benign lesion
  • 4 – possible malignant lesion
  • 5 – lesion highly suggestive for mgn
  • 6 – histological proven malignancy

BI-RADS #69

  • 0 – supplementary ex.
  • 1, 2 – normal screening programme
  • 3 – control (6 months)
  • 4 – biopsy
  • 5 – biopsy
  • 6 – therapy

Breast pathology #70

  • Benign lesions
  • - cyst
  • - fibroadenomas
  • Malignant lesions
  • - ductal carcinoma
  • - DCIS (ductal carcinoma in situ)
  • - IDC (invasive ductal carcinoma)
  • - lobular carcinoma
  • - LCIS (lobular carcinoma in situ) – high risk lesion!!!!
  • - ILC (invasive lobular carcinoma)

Breast cysts #71

  • Mx – circumscribed nodular density, round/oval, with rim calcifications
  • US – anechoic lesions, circumscribed, posterior enhancement
  • MRI – T2 – circumscribed lesion, hypersignal

Fibroadenomas #72

  • Mx – circumscribed nodular density, oval, can have “pop corn” calcifications
  • US –hypoechoic lesion, homogeneous, circumscribed, parallel to the skin
  • MRI – circumscribed, homogeneous / hyposignal septae, benign dynamic

DCIS #73

  • Mx – branching intraductal microcalcifications
  • US – dilated ducts with microcalcifications/hypoechoic content
  • MRI – low sensitivity (non-mass hypersignal)

DCIS #74

  • Mx – branching intraductal microcalcifications
  • US – dilated ducts with microcalcifications/hypoechoic content
  • MRI – low sensitivity (non-mass hypersignal)

IDC #75

  • Mx –nodular density with malignant features
  • US –hypoechoic mass with malignant features
  • MRI – mass with hypersignal after CM, with morphology and dynamic suggestive for malignancy

IDC #76

  • Mx –nodular density with malignant features
  • US –hypoechoic mass with malignant features
  • MRI – mass with hypersignal after CM, with morphology and dynamic suggestive for malignancy

ILC (frequently multicentric/multifocal, polyimorpf/multiform) #77

  • Mx – ocult/spiculated mass/architectural distortion/focal asimetry
  • US – irregular mass with shadowing/aria of shadowing
  • MRI – spiculated mass, with architectural distorsion

Interventional diagnosis and therapeutical manoeuvres #78

  • Diagnostic
  • - FNAB (for cysts)
  • - breast microbiopsy (tru-cut)
  • - vacuum assisted biopsy (macrobiopsy)
  • Treatment
  • - FNAB (cyst aspiration)
  • - vacuum assisted biopsy (lesions<1,5 cm)
  • - placing of tissue markers
  • - preoperative localisation (hook wires)
  • - sentinel node biopsy
  • Guiding method
  • - rontgen (stereotaxy)
  • - US
  • - MRI
